subject: Detection in N-mixture models when survey counts are highly correlated

messages.author: 1c5e51fb56f7a10c
messages.subject: Detection in N-mixture models when survey counts are highly correlated
parts:
Hi all,

I am using two-pass visual surveys to estimate fish abundance using N-mixture models. I have 79 sites that were surveyed twice, and among-site counts range from 0 to 400 or so. 

We have a high correlation of counts between passes at a given site (r2 = 0.97), and relatively little variation in our between-survey detection covariates. If I am following the AHM book (p. 224), am I correct in interpreting that the model has to (whether right or wrong) predict high detection under these conditions? 

Estimated detection was high when using ZIP and Poisson distributions, but data were still overdispersed. Only the NB distribution lowers c-hat to < 4. However, we run into issues when using NB (the model is non-identifiable) that have been outlined elsewhere.

Thanks,
Andy

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Detection in N-mixture models when survey counts are highly correlated
parts:
hi Andy,
 It should not necessarily predict high detection under these conditions.  One would expect it to produce unbiased estimates of detection if the model is properly specified.  That said, with counts in the range of 0 - 400 the core model assumptions are probably very tenuous and I would not expect the N-mixture model to do well in this situation, i.e., with a lot of over-dispersion, which is what you seem to be discovering.   I don't have any specific recommendations to dealing with that problem other than mark a subset of fish.
regards
andy
